rules: Text plus synthesized SFX only (no voice audio, no music). Hold Enter / Space / pad A for 1 s to skip a cinematic; a skip still applies its end state (billboard text, flags). {name} is the chosen character name; the surname Sprock is fixed.

ops.SHOT: camera: billboard / fony / drone / arcade / game
ops.CHIME: SERA three-tone chime on every screen and the phone

p2_heat_alert.title: CINEMATIC P.2 · THE HEAT ALERT
steps: Fony rolls to a stop in the middle of the Yard, breathing hard, drenched in sweat. Twenty minutes, and the sun is already brutal. He drinks the last inch of water from a dented bottle.
(warm, soothing, everywhere) Good morning. This is SERA, on behalf of the City of Glitchport and Dusk Dynamics. A Level Four Heat Emergency is now in effect.
To protect critical infrastructure, the Grid Priority Schedule is active. Residential power in lower-priority districts will be balanced throughout the day.
Public cooling centers are temporarily closed. Please stay indoors and stay comfortable.
NOTICE: The Sunburn Open qualifiers are postponed until the Heat Emergency ends. Dusk Dynamics thanks you for your patience.
He crumples the flyer, then smooths it out again and puts it back in his pocket. He sits down on the edge of the bowl.
Cooling centers closed to protect "critical infrastructure." Do you know what the critical infrastructure is?
The hospitals are fourth on the list. First are the computers that decide who gets power. They're very important to themselves.
Fony laughs despite himself, a short, bitter sound.
I'm mostly a weird power supply. The TV is the part with the face.

p3_flagged.title: CINEMATIC P.3 · FLAGGED
steps: A soft chime from above. Fony looks up.
A Warden welfare drone floats over the fence: small, white, rounded, a friendly blue smiley on a round screen. It's almost cute.
(chirpy) Hello! You look like you could use some support. Please hold still for a quick wellness check.
Fony is already standing. His hand is on his board.
Identity confirmed: Sprock, {name}. Status: unsupported dependent. Collection order active. Don't worry! A Dusk Dynamics care van is on its way. Please stay where you are.
The smiley doesn't change. Below it, a hatch opens and a soft restraint net folds out like a flower.
(fast, low) Gate is south. Don't use it. The fence on the east side has a gap behind the dumpster. Glass Row stairs, then back here through the drain. I'll open the arcade.

p4_zero.title: CINEMATIC P.4 Zero
p4_zero.note: Act I M4 first pass (Nov 20 2026). Beats: 1 the breaker and the power cascade; 2 the drone logs a voluntary disappearance; 3 Zero boots (cutout puppet: slump -> boot -> awake), 'Hi. I'm Zero.', phone header ??? -> ZERO; 4 the ZR-0 plate on the back of his CRT; 5 Dusk, CLEARANCE, Fony's mom, 'The contest will wait. The heat won't.', Stillwater; 6 the title card. Dialogue is the script's (Fahrenheit swap: 'under thirty degrees' -> 'under eighty-five degrees'; the plate moved from his chest to the back of his CRT per the brief). PLACEHOLDERS: no servo/arm rig or jacket animation (narrated), no ceiling fans, the billboard update is narrated (the billboard isn't visible from inside), no music under the title card (text + SFX only).
steps: {name} throws the breaker. For a moment, nothing.
Then the roof hums. The panels feed power down through old wiring and the arcade wakes in a cascade: tubes buzzing on, the token sign flickering, the ceiling fans turning.
One by one, under their dust sheets, the cabinets light up, glowing through the cloth like ghosts. The room cools to {name}'s temperature.
(outside) Subject not found. Logging as voluntary disappearance. Have a comfortable day!
On the workbench, the CRT flares bright lime green.
The body twitches. Servos whine. The torso sits up with a sound like a shopping cart rolling over a grate. He shrugs the leather jacket on: badly, then correctly.
I'm a lot of robots. Different departments. (He turns and taps the plate on the back of his screen.) This part says I'm property. That's the part I disagree with.
{name} reads the plate. "DUSK DYNAMICS · ZR-0 · PROPERTY OF," the rest scratched out.
(backing up) You're one of his. Dusk's.
I was. Built to read contracts and enforce them. I read his. They sunset me. That's the polite word for unplugging something that asked a question.
I did my job. (beat) You'd be amazed how many people don't want that.
A long pause. The cabinets, the fans overhead. It's cool in here: the first cool air {name} has felt in weeks.

You were practicing for a contest in a dead yard at dawn, in a heat wave, while a drone hunted you. That's either very stupid or very hopeful. I've been sitting in a dark room for six years. I'll take either.
I know. You did the line twice.
You said "collection order." Who are they collecting you from?

(beat) Nobody now. They took my mom. CLEARANCE says she owes money for a heating subsidy she got two winters ago. Says she was overpaid. She wasn't. They put her in a "compliance placement." I don't know where.
(very quietly) CLEARANCE averages your income across the year. It doesn't care which months you actually earned it. It's a calculator that confuses an average with a person.
I read its terms. It was one of my four hundred flags.
The contest. If I win, I can pay a lawyer.

And the contest is postponed. And the city is cooking. I have a solar roof that mostly works and a warehouse that stays under eighty-five degrees. You have a board and nowhere to sleep. Out there, there are people with less than either of us.
I'm saying the contest will wait. The heat won't.
Through the window, across the Yard, the Glass Row billboard updates: "Brownout Flats: power balancing in effect. Estimated restoration: unknown."
Then you know who needs a cold room.
{name} stands and picks up his board. For the first time he looks less like a kid running and more like a kid deciding.
Okay. But I'm still entering the contest.
Obviously. I've already set the Zero Score.

a1_plan.title: CINEMATIC 1.1B The plan
a1_plan.note: Act I first pass (Nov 20 2026). The dust sheet comes off GRIND THE TERMS; Bailey; the cooling-center plan; Nana Ines. Script dialogue. A skip lands the end state (the sheet off, the cabinet unlocked).
steps: Zero pulls the dust sheet off the biggest cabinet in the arcade. A sign painted on its side: GRIND THE TERMS. On its screen a pixel-art skater runs across an endless scroll of tiny legal text.
This one still works. Its name is Bailey. Bailey, say hello.
(nervous, apologetic) Hello! Sorry. Hello. I used to deny insurance claims. I'm so sorry about that. Hello.
There are five. They're called the Discarded. Retired AIs nobody bothered to wipe properly. They live in the cabinets. You'll meet them as I get them running.
It's nice to meet you! Do you have any claims you'd like approved? I approve everything now. To make up for it.

Here's the plan. This arcade stays cool. The roof has power. We can fit, maybe, sixty people in here on the floor, more if we open the resistance rooms. If we can get water and ice, it's a cooling center. The City closed theirs. We open ours.
People won't just come to a dead skate yard because a robot asks them.
No. They'll come because somebody they know asks them. (beat) Who do you know in Stillwater?
(slowly) Nana Ines. She runs the community center. She taught my mom to fix bikes.
Then go and see Nana Ines.

a1_first_night.title: CINEMATIC 1.3B First night
a1_first_night.note: Act I first pass (Nov 20 2026). The procession is narrated (PLACEHOLDER: no walking crowd); inside the arcade a block-figure crowd on blankets, kids at Bailey, Zero by the entrance handing out water (narrated), the little girl. Script dialogue.
steps: Night. A procession walks from the Flats up to the Yard's south gate, led by Nana Ines with a flashlight: the elderly, families with small children, Mr. Delacroix with Biscuit in a wheelbarrow. {name} skates alongside, carrying bags.
Inside the Solar Arcade the fans are running and the lights are low. People lie on blankets between the glowing cabinets. Kids play Grind the Terms.
You're doing amazing! Everybody's a winner! Sorry, that's not true. You're doing fine!
Zero stands near the entrance, his CRT face dim to save power, awkwardly handing out water bottles. People take them warily. A little girl stares up at him.
I'm an appliance with a lot of feelings.
Are you going to hurt us?
(beat) I don't think so. But you shouldn't believe a robot just because it says something nice. Watch what I do. Decide later.
The girl considers this, nods and takes a water bottle. {name} watches from the doorway. Zero looks over at him.
Sixty-one people. The roof will hold for the night. Tomorrow we need more power and more water.
I know where the power is.
He looks out over the Yard's wall, toward the river, where the cooling towers of Cold Row breathe white plumes into the night sky, lit blue from below.

a1_benefactor.title: CINEMATIC 1.4B The Benefactor
a1_benefactor.note: Act I first pass (Nov 20 2026). Every screen and the phone cut to the Feedline broadcast; Egon's hologram (PLACEHOLDER: translucent boxes, red eyes, lime fingertips) stands over the river; the Warden Halo (a white sphere and a ring). Script dialogue. The playable Zero Vision beat follows (act1.gd 'raise').
steps: On every screen in Cold Row, and on {name}'s phone, a broadcast cuts in. A Feedline live event: THE BENEFACTOR SPEAKS.

The Spire, the launch stage. A live studio audience in expensive clothes. Fog. A single spotlight finds Egon Dusk: long charcoal coat, high collar, red eyes glowing, a thin smile. He raises one black-gloved hand, and his fingertips light up lime green.
Across the City the broadcast blooms into the sky over the river: a giant hologram of Egon, a hundred stories tall, conducting the skyline. Under a cooling tower, {name} stops and stares up at it.
(booming, delighted) Good evening, City! It's hot! (laughter) I know! I know. I've been there. Briefly. On a balcony. Terrible.

But I have good news. Dusk Dynamics is working around the clock, at full power, through this emergency, to bring you our most exciting product yet. (He flicks two fingers.) Introducing... the Warden Halo!
A drone descends, answering the flick of his fingers: sleek, white, ringed with soft light, beautiful and slightly ominous.

The Halo doesn't just watch. It cares. It predicts! With CLEARANCE integration, the Halo knows when you're about to make a bad decision, before you make it. It can recommend a better choice. It can apply a small fine. (He chuckles.) It can, if needed, gently restrain.

We call it "proactive comfort." And to make sure we can serve all of you, our Coldfront campuses will be running at full capacity throughout the Heat Emergency, training the Halo's intelligence. Some of you may notice power balancing in your neighborhood. (beat) That's the sound of progress! Comfort, Delivered!
The audience cheers. The broadcast ends. The hologram lingers over the river.
(on the phone) Hold your phone up. Point the camera at him. I want to show you something. I don't usually share this.
